units.source_excerpt: In this paper, we present a computerized model to predict future crime locations and probable residences for a serial criminal based on the locations and times of a sequence of past crimes.
units.function: Open with the two operational targets and their shared evidence base.

features.clause_structure: main purpose clause plus infinitive and evidence phrase
features.quantitative_role: defines targets and inputs before mathematics

units.reusable_pattern: In this paper, we present [artifact] to [target 1] and [target 2] based on [observations].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim success before naming the targets.
Do not imitate the crime-specific facts verbatim.

units.source_excerpt: We first create a 'road metric' in order to measure distances by automobile travel time.
units.function: Introduce the shared technical object before either downstream model.

features.clause_structure: short main clause plus purpose infinitive

units.reusable_pattern: We first create [shared representation] in order to measure [domain quantity].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a proxy exact travel time without calibration.
Do not hide units behind a coined term.

units.source_excerpt: In order to predict future crime locations, we apply the nonparametric statistical technique of kernel density estimation with our road metric, which allows us to estimate a time dependent probability distribution function.
units.function: Bind the first target to a named method and output object.

features.clause_structure: fronted purpose clause, main action, relative output clause

units.reusable_pattern: In order to [target], we apply [method] with [domain modification], which yields [output].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the output as calibrated probability unless normalization is shown.
Do not omit the modification that distinguishes the method.

units.source_excerpt: In order to predict the residences of serial criminals, we use a refinement of a model developed by Rossmo, again adapting it to the road metric.
units.function: Present the second target in deliberately parallel syntax.

features.clause_structure: fronted purpose clause plus participial modification
features.quantitative_role: names model lineage and common metric

units.reusable_pattern: In order to [second target], we use a refinement of [base model], again adapting it to [shared representation].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply that adaptation preserves calibration.
Do not copy proper names where a different base model is used.

units.source_excerpt: We apply our model to several high profile serial murder cases, namely the case of Peter Sutcliffe, the 'Yorkshire Ripper' and that of Wayne Williams, the 'Atlanta Child Murderer.'
units.function: Close the method sequence by naming concrete evaluation cases.

features.clause_structure: main clause followed by appositive examples

units.reusable_pattern: We apply [model] to [case class], namely [case A] and [case B].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not convert two cases into broad validation.
Do not imitate sensational labels when they are irrelevant.

units.source_excerpt: Our model takes highway systems into account as a significant determiner of how criminals behave.
units.function: State the domain mechanism that motivates the paper's central representation.

features.clause_structure: compact transitive clause

units.reusable_pattern: Our model takes [domain structure] into account as a determinant of [behavior].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim causality without evidence.
Do not substitute domain vocabulary for a defined variable.

units.source_excerpt: Specifically, we created a road metric to give a measure of the time it takes for a driver to travel between two points on a map.
units.function: Turn the broad mechanism claim into one defined modeling object.

features.clause_structure: adverbial transition plus action and purpose clause

units.reusable_pattern: Specifically, we created [object] to measure [operational quantity] between [entities].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not equate a designed cost with observed time.
Do not omit the entities joined by the metric.

units.source_excerpt: We incorporate this road metric into several different models to give an estimate of where future crimes may occur and where the perpetrator may live.
units.function: Reconnect the common representation to both target branches.

features.clause_structure: main clause plus paired where complements
features.quantitative_role: maps one metric to two outputs

units.reusable_pattern: We incorporate [shared object] into [models] to estimate [target 1] and [target 2].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not blur different target variables into one output.
Do not claim fusion merely because inputs are shared.

units.source_excerpt: The beginning of our paper will be devoted to presenting the theoretical framework and an outline of our computer implementation. The later sections of our paper will be devoted to applying our model to famous notable criminal cases and assessing the accuracy of the model.
units.function: Make the theory-to-application document trajectory explicit.

features.clause_structure: two parallel sentences contrasting beginning and later sections

units.reusable_pattern: The beginning presents [framework/implementation]; the later sections apply it to [cases] and assess [criterion].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise accuracy without defining its measure.
Do not include a roadmap that the body does not follow.

units.source_excerpt: Develop the 'road metric' ... Estimate and extrapolate probability density functions ... Estimate offender's residence using a best fit circle under the road metric and by applying a modification of current models.
units.function: Compress the whole workflow into three parallel imperative stages.

features.clause_structure: three parallel verb-led list items

units.reusable_pattern: [Construct common representation]; [estimate target A]; [estimate target B using the common representation].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the list as proof that outputs are fused.
Do not vary grammatical form across parallel stages.

units.section: 2 Mapping Crime and the Road Metric
units.source_excerpt: We treat the highway system as a graph, considering each highway entrance and exit as a vertex in the graph, and each road section in between a pair of entrances and exits as an edge of the graph.
units.function: Translate a physical network into graph primitives in one sentence.

features.clause_structure: main mapping plus two parallel participial definitions

units.reusable_pattern: We treat [system] as a graph, considering [objects] as vertices and [connections] as edges.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit directionality or edge semantics when material.
Do not call a hand-built graph measured data.

units.source_excerpt: The road metric measures distances within a region based on the approximate total travel time by car.
units.function: Give the constructed metric a plain-language operational interpretation.

features.clause_structure: simple definition sentence

units.reusable_pattern: The [metric] measures [relation] within [scope] based on the approximate [operational cost].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim measured travel time when only length is used.
Do not drop the approximation qualifier.

units.source_excerpt: Time spent on side streets is proportional to the Manhattan metric ... Time spent on the freeway is proportional to the Euclidean distance.
units.function: Expose a piecewise cost assumption through balanced parallel statements.

features.clause_structure: two parallel proportionality clauses

units.reusable_pattern: Cost on [mode A] is proportional to [metric A], whereas cost on [mode B] is proportional to [metric B].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call proportionality calibrated without data.
Do not mix quantities with incompatible units silently.

units.source_excerpt: For each vertex v ... we compute the Manhattan distances ... For each pair of vertices v1, v2, we apply Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest path ... Then our road metric is defined as ...
units.function: Lead the reader from local connectors to network paths and finally the combined metric.

features.clause_structure: numbered parallel steps ending in a definition
features.transition: For each; For each pair; Then

units.reusable_pattern: For each [local object], compute [connector]; for each pair, compute [network path]; then define [metric] as the minimum combined cost.
reusable_elements: algorithm named at point of use
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip graph construction inputs.
Do not describe a route cost without its alternatives.

units.source_excerpt: In terms of actually computing the road metric, we divided the maps into m x n grids and computed and then stored the distance from each grid space to each other grid space.
units.function: Separate mathematical definition from the implemented discretization.

features.clause_structure: fronted implementation phrase plus coordinated operations

units.reusable_pattern: In actually computing [object], we discretized [domain] into [grid] and precomputed [pairwise quantity].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit cell size and extent in a reproducible paper.
Do not equate grid precision with empirical accuracy.

units.source_excerpt: In the case of Euclidean distances, given a set of sample points ... one often estimates the probability density function as ... This naturally presents an application of our road metric by replacing the Gaussian function K ... with the modified Gaussian function, G.
units.function: Introduce a standard baseline and then specify the domain substitution.

features.clause_structure: baseline exposition followed by This-led inference

units.source_excerpt: where d is the road metric defined above, and h is essentially an indirect control of the covariance of this kernel and Mi is the normalizing constant defined by ...
units.function: Define every new component immediately after the displayed kernel.

units.reusable_pattern: where [symbol] is [definition], [parameter] controls [shape], and [constant] normalizes [object].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a bandwidth covariance without dimensional checking.
Do not leave the integration domain implicit in a final specification.

units.source_excerpt: We treat h as a function of time since it is reasonable to assume that more recent crimes are more useful in predicting future crimes than earlier crimes and hence it is reasonable to let the modified Gaussian functions 'diffuse' over time by letting h be an increasing function.
units.function: Connect a behavioral recency premise to the direction of a model parameter.

units.reusable_pattern: We let [parameter] vary with [driver] since [domain premise], and hence choose [directional behavior].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat plausibility as calibration.

units.source_excerpt: Our above discussion gives a reasonable idea of where crimes have been committed, but it is not necessarily reasonable to expect that a criminal will distribute his or her crimes based on a single probability distribution function for all time. Therefore we decided to perform a weighted least squares approximation based on trends in the probability distribution functions discussed above.
units.function: Use a limitation of the static field to motivate the temporal extrapolation layer.

features.clause_structure: contrastive sentence followed by Therefore sentence

units.reusable_pattern: The current model describes [known state], but [limitation]; therefore we apply [extension] to [new target].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add complexity without naming the failed assumption.
Do not call extrapolated values valid probabilities without constraints.

units.source_excerpt: In our equation for phi(x,t) ... we sum over only the crimes which have occurred before time t ... We now do a weighted least squares approximation to estimate phi(x,t*).
units.function: Turn the extrapolation concept into a temporal-information-respecting procedure.

features.clause_structure: ordered bullet sequence with equations

units.reusable_pattern: Restrict inputs to [available history], construct [intermediate states], then fit [estimator] to obtain [future output].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use future event information in an operational backtest.

units.source_excerpt: One common method for estimating the residence of a serial criminal is to treat the location of each crime as a point mass and find the centroid of the point masses by means of a spacial average.
units.function: Introduce the residence branch from a familiar baseline method.

features.clause_structure: copular frame plus infinitive operations

units.reusable_pattern: One common method for [target] is to represent [data] as [objects] and compute [summary].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply common use proves suitability.
Do not omit the metric underlying the center.

units.source_excerpt: This is based on the assumption that criminals will typically try to avoid committing crimes very near to where they live, but at the same time will expend roughly the same amount of effort in each of their crimes.
units.function: State the competing behavioral forces before presenting the circle model.

features.clause_structure: that-clause with but-at-the-same-time balance

units.reusable_pattern: The model assumes [force A], but at the same time [force B].
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present behavioral assumptions as observed fact.
Do not omit plausible alternative mechanisms.

units.source_excerpt: The most naive thing we could do is fit a circle to the data by minimizing the square of the distance from our crime locations to a circle ... Unfortunately this method is very unstable.
units.function: Make the rejected first formulation explicit before replacing it.

units.reusable_pattern: A first attempt minimizes [simple objective]. Unfortunately, this formulation is [specific failure].

units.source_excerpt: Consider the example in Figure 1 of the best fit circle for three points. Moving the middle point slightly produces a tremendous change in the best fit circle's radius and center.

units.section: 4.2.2 A More Refined Best Fit Circle
units.source_excerpt: This provides a natural generalization to the road metric which is perhaps a better extension of the often used method of centrography. Namely, we define the center of our best fit circle to be the point x such that ... is minimized.
units.function: Replace the failed circle fit with a metric-space center and qualify the choice.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a generalized center a jointly fitted circle unless radius residuals are optimized.

units.source_excerpt: In this section we apply the models discussed earlier to two notable cases, namely the Yorkshire Ripper (Peter Sutcliffe) and the Atlanta Child Murderer (Wayne Williams).
units.function: Open results by binding prior methods to two named parallel cases.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a small case set representative.

units.source_excerpt: There were a total of 20 criminal incidents committed by Sutcliffe. We ran our density distribution model on the first 19 cases in order to predict the location of the 20th.
units.function: State the denominator and holdout split before reporting the map.

features.clause_structure: count sentence followed by protocol sentence

prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide that only one event is held out.

units.source_excerpt: If one were to use our model in real life, the time of the next crime would not actually be known, but this is not of great importance since our choice of the variance function in our kernel causes the model to stabilize very quickly.
units.function: Surface a deployment mismatch immediately beside the test protocol.

units.source_excerpt: From our extrapolated probability distribution, the 20th attack was 8.58 times more likely to occur in the cell containing the actual murder site than it was to occur in an average square. More importantly, the result of our model would direct law enforcement officers to begin their search in precisely the square where the murder occurred.
units.function: Move from a numerical relative score to its stated decision consequence.

units.source_excerpt: Although Rossmo's model did not generate a hotspot directly on Sutcliffe's residence, it still provided a good starting point for a police investigation. Sutcliffe's house was on a second or third priority band and would be located reasonably quickly in a search effort.

units.source_excerpt: One of the most novel aspects of our approach was the design of the road metric to accurately estimate the cost of travel to a criminal. units.source_excerpt: As we observed in the case of the Atlanta Child Murderer, the kernel method was unable to predict a relatively unexpected kill site ... We may be able to improve our model by skewing our probability distribution toward areas with high concentrations of potential victims.

units.source_excerpt: As each distance computation requires an application of Dijkstra's algorithm, the determination of all of these distances is quite slow. units.source_excerpt: The kernel method was particularly viable in the Sutcliffe case, most likely due to the tendency of attacks to cluster. However, it became less accurate as attacks spread out more uniformly.

units.source_excerpt: In our paper we present a computerized model for predicting future crimes and estimating the location of a criminal based on the location and times of past crimes. The model is based on geographic profiling and makes heavy use of the local highway systems near to the crimes.

units.source_excerpt: For our model to be useful, it must be applied to cases where the location of crimes has been determined ... Secondly, our model is most useful if applied to relatively small areas ... and thus should be applied primarily to cases where the perpetrator is suspected of using an automobile.

units.source_excerpt: Our model makes two predictions. Firstly it gives an estimate of where future crimes will occur ... It does not give an accurate estimate for the absolute probability that an offender will be within a particular region, but instead provides the locations of hotspots where law enforcement should begin its investigation.

units.source_excerpt: Secondly, our model makes an estimate based on Rossmo's model. This approach balances two factors affecting the distance a criminal travels to commit a crime. units.source_excerpt: Empirical tests of our model on high profile criminal cases has shown that both of these methods give useful starting points for investigation. We recommend that your officers apply our techniques to complement the other methods at their disposal.
